subject: Clarify invite links for Dec 14 demo — Meet/Zoom duplicate causing guest rejects
body:
From: Kelly Barnes <kelly@fintechplus.com>
To: mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 20:08:00 +0000
Subject: Demo confirmation and weird calendar links

Hi Mina,

Thanks for scheduling the demo for Dec 14 at 10:00am PT. I just created the Google Calendar invite and included our external stakeholders, but two things popped up: 1) the invite shows both a Google Meet link and a Zoom link in the description, and 2) two attendees from our payments team (sam.patel@fintechplus.com and another external) are getting a "This event is blocked by your domain" error when they try to RSVP/join.

Quick question — can you confirm which link Redwood wants everyone to use? Also, if you can resend a single canonical .ics with only the Zoom join and an updated organizer email (redwood-demo@redwood.ai) that might prevent our domain calendar policies from injecting Meet.

Attachments: original-invite.ics (text/calendar), screenshot-mixed-links.png (image/png)

Thanks,
Kelly Barnes
Head of Product Operations
FintechPlus

-----

On Fri, 11 Dec 2026 at 21:03 +0000, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai> wrote:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Kelly Barnes <kelly@fintechplus.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 21:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Demo confirmation and weird calendar links

Hi Kelly — thanks for flagging this.

We're seeing two common failure modes here: some calendar providers auto-add a Meet link when a Google-origin event is detected, and some corporate calendar proxies enforce domain routing (they rewrite or block invites that come from external organizer addresses). The cleanest fix is for us to:

- Send a fresh .ics from a Redwood-controlled organizer (redwood-demo@redwood.ai) that contains only the Zoom join URL in the location/description fields.
- Paste the Zoom join (https://zoom.us/j/9123456789) explicitly in the event body so clients use that.
- For any guests reporting the domain-block error, please send their exact emails and I will ask our calendar team to whitelist or send them an individual calendar-forward.

I can reissue an invite right now and CC your attendees — do you want me to: (A) replace the existing event, or (B) send a new event and ask participants to decline the old one? Option B is lower risk across heterogeneous calendars.

I will also loop in our infra person to check whether the original invite included both conferencing options (Google sometimes attaches both).

— Mina
Mina Haddad
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0183

-----

On Sat, 12 Dec 2026 at 08:12 +0000, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai> wrote:
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 08:12:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Demo confirmation and weird calendar links

Looping in calendar infra — we see patterns like this when the organizer creates an event in GCal and both the Meet and a third-party conferencing (Zoom) add-in were active on the browser. That can generate duplicated conferencing metadata in the .ics (GEO/URL/CONFERENCE entries). Some corporate proxies then rewrite the event and insert a Meet link, which causes conflicts.

Connor/Marcus — can you:
- Check the original-invite.ics in the Drive link and confirm whether both a MEET and a ZOOM conference element are present.
- If so, generate a sanitized .ics with only the Zoom conference block and the Zoom join URL in the description.
- Reissue the event from redwood-demo@redwood.ai and include the FintechPlus attendees as explicit guests (not via group).

I've attached calendar-diagnostics.log from our CalConnector service.

Attachments: calendar-diagnostics.log (text/plain)

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Success Ops
Redwood Inference

-----

On Sat, 12 Dec 2026 at 17:45 +0000, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai> wrote:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 17:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Demo confirmation and weird calendar links

Thanks — dug into the .ics and confirmed both CONFERENCE-MEET and an X-ZOOM block existed. That happens when the browser add-on is toggled while creating the event. I've sanitized the .ics (new-invite-zoom.ics) and reissued the event from redwood-demo@redwood.ai.

Steps I took:
- Created new event under redwood-demo@redwood.ai (our shared organizer).
- Put Zoom join URL in both the LOCATION and the BODY fields: https://zoom.us/j/9123456789
- Cleared any MEET or X-MEET metadata from the .ics.
- Sent the invite to Kelly, Sam Patel, and the listed stakeholders.

Attached the new-invite-zoom.ics. For affected FintechPlus users who still see an error, we recommend they accept the invite via the Zoom link directly and then manually add to their calendar — their domain proxy appears to be rewriting inbound calendar events.

Connor O'Brien
Platform Reliability — Infra
Redwood Inference
connor_obrien@redwood.ai

Attachments: new-invite-zoom.ics (text/calendar)

-----

On Sun, 13 Dec 2026 at 02:15 +0000, Kelly Barnes <kelly@fintechplus.com> wrote:
From: Kelly Barnes <kelly@fintechplus.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sam Patel <sam.patel@fintechplus.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 13 Dec 2026 02:15:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Demo confirmation and weird calendar links

Mina/Connor/Laura — confirmed. We received the new redwood-demo invite and the Zoom-only ICS. Sam and the payments folks were able to join when they used the Zoom link directly; the calendar proxy at FintechPlus still shows the old blocked event in some mailboxes but we've asked affected users to delete that event and accept the new one.

All good on our side. See you on Dec 14 at 10am PT.

Thanks for the fast turnaround.

Kelly Barnes
Head of Product Operations
FintechPlus

-----

Thread notes: original issue caused by mixed conferencing metadata in .ics + domain calendar rewrite. Resolution: reissue from shared redwood-demo organizer with sanitized .ics and explicit Zoom URL.
